chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from al-Mansur ibn Yunus, from Jalis for Abu Hamzah, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him):
The Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Everything is perishable but He (His Face).'

(1) He (AS) replied: Everything will perish, but the Face will remain. Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, is Greater than being attributed with a face. However, the meaning of this is that everything will perish except His Religion and the Face from which He bestows.

key_terms.الْوَجَهُ: The Face (of Allah, interpreted here as meaning or source rather than physical form)

ai.seo_question: What does 'His Face' mean in the Quranic verse 'Everything is perishable but His Face'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that 'Face' (Wajh) in this verse denotes Allah's eternal essence and His Religion (Din), rather than a physical attribute, thereby affirming divine transcendence (Tanzih) against anthropomorphism. This interpretation highlights that all created things are transient, while the divine command and the path to Him remain perpetual, offering believers a concrete spiritual anchor in the face of worldly impermanence.
